title: Long-context model split-streaming vs reshard: latency and throughput tradeoffs
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a set of microbenchmarks and runbook-style notes for serving very long-context models (32k+ tokens) across multi-GPU inference clusters. We're comparing two practical approaches for keeping KV state and activations in-check: (A) split-streaming (gradual KV streaming of recent windows + local short-lived KV caches), and (B) periodic resharding (repartitioning model state periodically so each request touches fewer remote devices). The goal is realistic guidance for routing, scheduling, and fallback policies when latency SLOs are tight and contexts are long.

Background / motivation:
- Customers are adopting >32k context models. Memory + KV-cache blowups cause either graph reloading or cross-node fetches.
- Existing per-request all-kv-localization strategies are costly or impossible with limited memory per GPU.
- Two high-level strategies exist in our stack; we need empirical tradeoffs to form default config for hosted and dedicated offerings.

Definitions / approaches evaluated:
- Split-streaming (SS): stream only a moving window of recent tokens (e.g., last 8k tokens) to the serving job while older context is summarized or stored in an external chunk store. During generation we prefetch adjacent chunks lazily and keep a tiny local KV cache per session.
- Periodic Reshard (PR): reshard model KV + activations such that the working set of a particular request is concentrated on fewer GPUs. This implies a transient reshard/relayout step at checkpoint load or at request start (costly) but reduces cross-node KV lookups during actual token generation.
- Hybrid heuristics: SS+PR with lightweight prefetch (PR for top-k hot shards, SS for tail chunks). We included one hybrid variant in the tests.

Cluster / infra baseline used for experiments:
- Node: 8x A100-80GB NVLink-per-node (two nodes in rack), Mellanox HDR200, PCIe Gen4, CPU: 2x 64-core, Ubuntu 22.04, OFED 5.5
- Software: runtime-nightly-2025-02-10 build, NCCL 2.17, our KV-store prototype (s3-like chunk store simulated), RDMA reads used for streaming experiments, kernel tweaks: doorbell coalescing enabled for some runs.
- Model: 70B transformer with 64k context synthetic weights and two variants: 'dense-kv' (heavy KV footprint) and 'sparse-kv' (sharded keys but sparser access).

Workloads:
- Single large-session generation: 1 session with 64k context, generate 1k new tokens at 0.5–2 tokens/s pacing.
- Multi-small-sessions: 200 concurrent sessions, each with 8k context, bursty generation with random inter-arrival times (peaky traffic).
- Mixed: 20 large sessions + 300 small sessions to stress multi-tenancy.

Metrics collected:
- P99/P95 token latency; median latency; time spent in reshuffle/reshard step; PCIe read bytes per second; RDMA ops/sec; NCCL allreduce time per step; CPU scheduling stalls; observed KV-cache hit ratio; outage/fallback frequency.

Summary of results (high level):
1) Split-streaming (SS):
   - Pros: Lower cold-start cost, minimal blocking at request start, graceful degradation—when a chunk isn't available we resume generation with a compact summary fallback.
   - Cons: During peaky workloads, RDMA burstiness produced microbursts of PCIe read traffic and host staging that increased p99 tail by ~1.8–2.5x versus median. KV-cache hit ratio depended heavily on window size; 8k window mapped to ~73% hit for our synthetic traces.
   - Numbers: single large-session p95 token latency ~45ms (steady), p99 ~130ms (peaks during prefetches). Multi-small-sessions p95 ~18ms, p99 ~90ms.

2) Periodic Reshard (PR):
   - Pros: When reshard completes, per-token latency dropped and NIC+PCIe activity during generation was much lower (fewer cross-node KV requests). P99 token latency after reshard similar to median for SS but with lower variance.
   - Cons: Reshard step is expensive: a full reshard for 64k context costs 1.8–2.6s (wall) depending on interconnect. That single large pause violates short SLOs; must be scheduled during warm periods or amortized across many sessions. PR also sharply increases memory pressure during reshard, occasionally blowing OOM on older nodes.
   - Numbers: generation token latency after reshard p50~40ms, p99~95ms. Reshard time variance dominated by NCCL all-to-all and host staging, and ranged 1.8s–2.6s on our infra.

3) Hybrid: SS+PR (selective resharding of hot shards)
   - Best tradeoff we saw: do a lightweight PR that remaps 20% of hot shards (hot-hot keys) and stream the rest. This reduced average p99 by ~25% compared to SS alone while keeping reshard pauses <700ms in most trials.

Profiling observations (interesting signals):
- Host staging hotspots: many of the prefetch patterns triggered repeated host->GPU DMA and doorbell flood, increasing CPU-side interrupt handling. We saw high ctx_switches and qlen growth on doorbell queues.
- RDMA burst collapse: under SS prefetches, RDMA traffic was bursty and when not paced caused NIC-level packet drops and retries, which amplified tail latency. Enabling pacing reduced p99 by ~20% at a cost of slightly higher median.
- NCCL collectives during reshard: reshard dominated by many-to-many collectives; tuning NCCL topo and switching to pairwise async transfers (experimental) reduced reshard time by ~25% at the cost of slightly higher steady-state token latency.
- Memory fragmentation: PR increases transient contiguous GPU memory needs which sometimes triggered fragmentation-induced serial compaction. This led to spikes where allocator fallback paths executed slow memcpy loops.

Microbench details and chosen knobs:
- SS prefetch window size sweep: {4k, 8k, 16k} tokens. Key result: 8k was sweet spot for our synthetic traces; 4k too low (cache hit <55%), 16k offered marginal hit gains and larger RDMA bursts.
- Prefetch pacing: immediate vs rate-limited vs adaptive (based on recent RDMA success). Adaptive pacing (targeted throughput + backoff on retransmit) reduced p99 considerably.
- PR granularity: full-reshard vs shard-group-reshard (group size 8 shards). Group sharding lowered pause time but increased steady-state cross-node traffic if groups mismatched hot keys.

Failure modes / operational notes:
- Uncoordinated reshard during autoscaler events sometimes collides with node eviction: we observed partial reshard + node terminate => inconsistent KV state and request failures. Need cluster-level barrier or transactional reshard commit.
- When SSD chunk store latency spikes (we simulated S3 blips) SS prefetch latency cascades. Recommend giving prefetch higher priority QoS to avoid starving active token gen.

Recommendations to product/ops:
1) Default hosted setting: enable Split-streaming with 8k default window + adaptive prefetch pacing. Add per-tenant knob to increase window if they pay for higher memory/dedicated capacity.
2) Offer PR as opt-in for dedicated customers who can accept minute-level warmup or during maintenance windows; add an option for "background reshard" that runs opportunistically on low-util nodes.
3) Implement hybrid auto-trigger: if KV cache miss rate > X% for Y seconds and session TTL > T, schedule a selective reshard of top-k shards.
4) Add metrics + alerts: reshard-duration histogram, prefetch-retry-rate, pdq_backoff_count, doorbell-queue-length, pci_read_amplification. Use these to auto-disable prefetch pacing when infra is congested.

Action items / next experiments:
- Run same suite on mixed GPU cluster (A100 + H100) to measure reshard cost variance and allocator impact. (Owner: Ethan, ETA 2025-03-05).
- Prototype transactional reshard commit that writes a reshard manifest and atomically flips mapping to avoid partial states. (Owner: Priya, ETA 2025-03-12).
- Try per-shard micro-checkpointing to reduce reshard walltime (experimental code in PR 987). (Owner: Luca, ETA 2025-03-08).

Open questions / discussion points:
- How to price resharding? If customers use PR heavily, it increases both infra churn and observable tails. Should be part of Dedicated SLAs only?
- Are there model-level tweaks (attention compression, sparse enabled checkpoints) we can upstream to model teams to make SS more effective?

Notes / references: linked artifacts above, Slack trace: #serving-runtime long-context thread 2025-02-14, Linear ticket RW-1342 for hybrid auto-trigger, perf PR: github/pr/987 includes micro-checkpoint prototype.

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call when a long-context session reports p99 degradation:
- Check doorbell queue lengths and PCIe read bytes for affected hosts.
- Inspect RDMA retransmit counters and NIC drops.
- If reshard in progress, check reshard manifest state and time elapsed; if > threshold abort and fall back to SS.
- Toggle prefetch pacing to limited mode via runtime flag and observe p99.
